findings.title: A cached denial can block newly granted access
findings.body: This returns a prior denial without rechecking current permissions. If a user was denied for a resource before it was created or before access was granted, the same request continues to be denied for the cache TTL (30 seconds), even though the database now allows it. This can prevent the newly created dashboards or folders this change is intended to make accessible from loading immediately.

findings.title: Denial cache key does not distinguish identity types
findings.body: The key identifies a principal only by its UID, but checks also support distinct identity types such as users and service accounts. If those identity namespaces contain the same UID, a denial cached for one identity will incorrectly deny the other identity's request for the same resource and action. Include the identity type in the key.

findings.title: Unescaped key components can collide
findings.body: The key concatenates the resource name and parent folder with underscores, so different valid name/folder pairs can produce the same key (for example, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c`). A denial for one resource can then incorrectly deny access to the other until the entry expires. Encode or delimit components unambiguously.
